reason: The PR fixes a JIT fastpass bug where an absent optional key whose custom check fails (and writes ctx.value) keeps the leaked value in the parsed output; before the fix safeParse({}) returns {success:true,data:{a:'leaked'}}, so the test's assertion that 'a' is absent fails.
After the fix the JIT fastpass drops the value alongside the swallowed issue, so safeParse({}) yields {success:true,data:{}} with no 'a' key, matching the test.

Before the fix marked swallows a tab-only middle line as a lazy continuation, merging two paragraphs into one (

foo\tbar

); the test expects two separate paragraphs.
The fix widens the paragraph continuation lookahead to treat a tab-only line as blank, so 'foo\n\t\nbar' yields two paragraphs as the test expects.
The PR only changes error-path stack decoration in Axios.js; it does not affect successful JSON response parsing, so the test's expected parsed-object behavior is unchanged and passes.
The change is confined to error handling and does not alter JSON response parsing on the success path, so the test still passes after the PR.
The PR only changes negative-number exponent handling in Commander's arg parser; boolean flag parsing is unaffected, so '--verbose' is still recognized as true with no error at base.
The change is confined to negative-number arg detection and does not affect boolean flag parsing, so the flag test still passes after the PR.
Before the fix JsonTreeReader.nextInt/nextLong silently coerce full-width digits to 123 via Integer.parseInt, so no parsing error is raised; the test expects a clear error, so it fails at base.
After the fix JsonTreeReader.nextInt/nextLong validate non-ASCII string tokens and throw MalformedJsonException, so the full-width-digit input raises the expected error.
Before the fix the alphanumeric-only regex splits 'test-db' into 'test' and 'db', setting search_path to two schemas; the test expects a single 'test-db', so it fails at base.
After the fix the delimiter-blocklist regex keeps 'test-db' intact, setting search_path to the single schema name as the test expects.
The PR only fixes a resource leak in ByteBufferUtil.fromStream; ImageView transformation eligibility is untouched, so the transformation is still applied by default at base.
The change is confined to buffer recycling in ByteBufferUtil and does not affect image transformation handling, so the test still passes after the PR.
The PR only caches the allowedSymbolsAndAlphanumerics set and the description/verification show identical violation counts (84/84, 0/0), so the allowed_symbols behavior is preserved at base.
The caching change preserves configuration behavior per the PR verification, so the allowed-symbol identifier still passes after the PR.
The PR merely adds a missing <cstdint> include for GCC 15 compilation; percent-encoded SVG data URI loading is unaffected, so the test passes at base.
The PR only adds Afrikaans 'week'/'weeks' locale strings; datetime hour-shift across DST arithmetic is unaffected, so the test passes after the PR.
The PR only adds a missing <cstdint> include for compilation; percent-encoded SVG data URI loading is unaffected, so the test passes after the PR.
The PR changes Cookie header directive parsing, which is unrelated to form-urlencoded content decoding of optional fields, so the empty-body decode still succeeds at base.
Cookie parsing changes do not affect form-urlencoded optional-field decoding, so the test still passes after the PR.
The PR only fixes spelling in a comment and a test variable name; Remove behavior for non-empty directories is unchanged, so the test passes at base.
Spelling-only changes do not alter directory-removal behavior, so the non-empty-dir removal is still rejected after the PR.
The PR fixes JSON encode flags/depth in a Json type test, unrelated to schema index comparison, so the diff comparison still completes without warnings at base.
The PR fixes JSON encode flags/depth in a Json type test, unrelated to schema index comparison, so the diff comparison still completes without warnings after the PR.
The PR only adds Afrikaans week/weeks locale strings; datetime hour-shift across DST arithmetic is unaffected, so the test passes at base.
The PR fixes a CircuitBreaker predicate permit leak; the rate limiter (a different module) is untouched, so its refresh/replenish behavior is unchanged at base.
CircuitBreaker changes do not affect the semaphore rate limiter, so the limiter still replenishes after a lowered limit after the PR.
The PR fixes an ASI hazard in the prefer-template rule's autofix, not the var/no-var rule; the var-autofix hoisting behavior tested here is unchanged at base.
The prefer-template ASI fix does not touch the var-rule autofix, so the block-scoped declaration hoisting behavior tested here is unchanged after the PR.
The PR fixes log-formatter arg mangling in scrapy/utils/log.py; SitemapSpider JOBDIR resume behavior is untouched, so the test passes at base.
Log-formatter changes do not affect SitemapSpider resume/restart behavior, so the test still passes after the PR.
The PR only changes --sanitize bidi-control substitution, which the test does not exercise (no --sanitize flag); double-width char rendering at narrow width is unaffected at base.
The bidi --sanitize fix is unrelated to the double-width/theme row-background narrow-terminal rendering path tested here, so it still passes after the PR.
The PR optimizes the RFC5424 syslog parser regex; the file-output symlink-per-key behavior is in a different plugin and is unaffected at base.
Syslog parser changes do not affect the file output plugin's per-key symlink maintenance, so the test still passes after the PR.
The PR changes ConcurrentBag's virtual-thread yield spin, unrelated to pool-name generation / System-properties locking, so the construction test passes at base.
ConcurrentBag virtual-thread spin changes do not affect system-property lock contention during pool-name generation, so the concurrency test still passes after the PR.
The PR fixes ACL key checks for the SORT command; 32-bit BGSAVE/RDB persistence is unaffected, so the background save succeeds at base.
SORT ACL key-check fixes do not affect background save on 32-bit Redis, so the BGSAVE test still passes after the PR.
The PR fixes CWD handling during nvim_win_set_buf context switches; CTRL-A number incrementing (edit.c) is untouched, so the 50-digit increment test passes at base.
The CWD-context fix does not affect CTRL-X number decrement behavior, so the 50-digit decrement test still passes after the PR.
The PR fixes an external file-cache block reclaim race; the || operator array-typing behavior is in a different subsystem and is unaffected at base.
File-cache race fix does not affect list/|| type agreement, so the test still passes after the PR.
The PR fixes ScrollBar touch drag handling; RefCounted _notification PREDELETE behavior is unaffected, so the test passes at base.
ScrollBar input handling changes do not affect RefCounted PREDELETE notification, so the release test still passes after the PR.
The PR adds a categorical+absolute_error error to DecisionTreeRegressor; f_regression constant-column handling is in feature_selection and is unaffected at base.
DecisionTree categorical error changes do not affect r_regression's near-constant column correlation, so the test still passes after the PR.
The PR fixes a swagger-ui readonly attribute in the UI; Vault Agent file-sink mode handling is untouched, so the 0640 sink test passes at base.
Swagger UI changes do not affect Vault Agent file-sink permission bits, so the 0600 sink test still passes after the PR.
Before the fix, HelpFormatter.write_usage with empty args emitted only a blank line (wrap_text discarded the prefix), so the first help line is not 'Usage: cli'; the test fails at base.
After the fix, write_usage emits the prefix line 'Usage: cli' with no args, and the new end-to-end tests assert exactly that, so the test passes at head.
The PR fixes IPv6 host/port parsing in run() and the test client; returning a dict as JSON is core Flask behavior and is unaffected at base.
IPv6 host parsing changes do not affect dict-to-JSON response serialization, so the test still passes after the PR.
The PR fixes unhashable generic-alias handling in schema generation; required-field validation is unaffected, so the missing-field error test passes at base.
Generic-alias schema fix does not affect required-field validation, so the test still passes after the PR.
logging.WARN and logging.WARNING are the same constant (30), so replacing it is a no-op for effective log levels; echo-off still suppresses INFO logging at base.
WARN and WARNING are identical constants, so the rename does not change log-level behavior and the echo test still passes after the PR.
The PR refactors method_missing for thread safety but generated attribute methods are cached after first access, so steady-state column read costs and the ratio are unchanged at base.
The thread-safe method_missing refactor still defines and caches attribute methods, so normal attribute reads remain fast and the ratio test still passes after the PR.

Before the fix, getCalledListeners iterated the per-dispatch $callStack, which contained one WrappedListener per invocation, so two dispatches yielded two entries matching the expected count of two at base.

The fix deliberately dedups called listeners ('the list only stores each listener once per event'), so after two dispatches getCalledListeners returns one entry, not the two the test expects; the test fails at head.
The PR only fixes shellcheck word-splitting in COMPREPLY assignment; subcommand custom-completion hook selection is unchanged, so each subcommand gets its own suggestions at base.
The shellcheck fixes do not alter which subcommand's completion hook runs, so the correct per-subcommand suggestions still appear after the PR.

The PR bumps qs to 6.14.0, which fixes repeated-key parsing; at base (qs 6.13.0) repeating the same key 25 times is reported to yield an object rather than the expected ordered array, so the test fails.
After bumping to qs 6.14.0 the repeated-key query parsing correctly returns an ordered array of all 25 values, matching the test expectation.
Before the change get_environ_proxies(url) took a single URL argument, so calling it with only the URL returns a dict and the test passes at base.
The PR changed the signature to get_environ_proxies(url, no_proxy) with no default for no_proxy, so calling it with only the URL raises a TypeError; the test fails at head.
The PR only makes parse_unit_value accept a leading '.' for valid units like .5sec; '.foons' has no valid unit, so it still returns None and '.foons' is parsed as a string at base.
With the guard relaxed, '.foons' is parsed as a number+unit; 'foons' is not a unit so parse_unit_value returns None and the token stays a string, so the test still passes after the PR.
Before the fix HEAD requests connected a temp-file sink (and with an Accept-Encoding/gzip path a HEAD response has no body), which caused a fatal error; the request failed at base.
After the fix HEAD requests no longer connect a sink, so a HEAD request with the Accept-Encoding header completes and returns a valid status without error.
At base a map in a match failure is simply inspected via the default escape branch, so assert :foo = %{bar: [1 | 2]} reports the match failure with the map shown and no crash.
After the PR maps are converted to AST and formatted by the map algebra, which already handles improper lists, so the match failure still formats cleanly without a crash.

Before the fix css_props registered a teardown that removed the element and hydration of dynamic css-prop components was broken, so the dynamically-selected inner component lost its --prop color / errored at base.
The PR removes the element-removing teardown and fixes dynamic-component hydration for css props, so the inner component keeps the red --prop color before and after the toggle.
At base the transform guard used plain code.includes('new URL') and includes('import.meta.url'), which succeed for the multi-line form, so the asset is emitted correctly.

At head the transform is gated by a hook filter regex /new\s+URL.+import\.meta\.url/ whose '.' does not match newlines, so the multi-line reference is skipped and the asset is never emitted (regression).
At base the preview child process is launched without any NUL-containing env var, so a NUL-delimited item's preview runs and shows 'ok'.
At head FZF_CURRENT_ITEM=item.AsString() includes the NUL bytes from the NUL-delimited item; an env value with embedded NUL makes the preview child process fail to start, so the test fails.
At base switching immersiveSticky to edgeToEdge applies setSystemUiVisibility with only LAYOUT_* flags, clearing the immersive hide flags so the system bars reappear.
At head the edgeToEdge branch only calls WindowCompat.setDecorFitsSystemWindows(false) and returns without clearing the immersive HIDE flags set by immersiveSticky, so the system bars stay hidden.
At base ruff has no multiple-assignment-in-case check, so case ClassLabel(num_classes=num_classes): (a valid single capture) passes cleanly.
At head the new visitor inserts both the keyword attr 'num_classes' and the capture name 'num_classes', treating the valid single binding as a duplicate and reporting a false syntax error.
At base decodeBodyToStruct does sli.Index(i).Set(v) without growing the slice, so for the 2nd block (i=1) on a length-1 slice it panics with slice/reflect index out of range.
The PR appends to the slice when i >= sli.Len(), so both blocks decode into a 2-entry slice without panic, matching the expected result.
At base mockConstructorParameters only sets timezone when $timezone is truthy; with setTestNow (no tz) the mocked now keeps America/Los_Angeles, so Carbon::now() returns laDate not utcDate.
At head it sets timezone to $timezone ?? date_default_timezone_get() (UTC), so Carbon::now() without a tz uses UTC and matches utcDate.

At base PROTOCOL_RELATIVE_REGEX=^[/\\]{2}[^/\\]+ requires exactly two leading slashes followed by a non-slash, so '///test.com', '/<tab>//...' and '/\/...' do not match (reported not protocol-relative).
At head PROTOCOL_RELATIVE_REGEX=^([/\\]\s*){2,}[^/\\] accepts 2+ slashes with optional whitespace, so all three are correctly classified as protocol-relative.

The PR only swaps asBytes() for getBytesInternal() inside combineOrdered/combineUnordered (a no-value-change micro-opt); MD5('abc') is independent of those helpers, so it still equals the standard digest at base.
Same reasoning as base: the refactor does not alter MD5 computation, so MD5('abc') still equals the standard digest at head.
The PR only relocates diagnostic descriptor definitions into a new class with identical codes/messages/severities; source generation of a GET client is unaffected at base.
The refactor keeps diagnostic codes/messages/severities unchanged, so GET client generation and the captured request are unaffected at head.
The PR removes only redundant trailing `continue` statements (no control-flow change), so a basic HTTP/1.1 GET with body still returns 200 with the correct body at base.
Removing the redundant `continue` does not change dispatch/body-reading behavior, so the HTTP/1.1 GET body check still passes at head.
At base to_iso8601/2 converts to ISO then calls to_iso8601() without the format, so the :basic request silently returns the :extended form '2001-01-01' instead of '20010101'.
The PR passes the requested format through (to_iso8601(format)), so to_iso8601(holo_date, :basic) returns '20010101'.
At base on PHP 8.2+ the native `end` property is not re-synced after setEndDate, so `end` still reports the original 2024-09-30 while getEndDate() reports 2025-06-15, failing the assertion.
The PR adds syncNativePeriod() which re-initializes the parent DatePeriod, so both `end` and getEndDate() report the newly set 2025-06-15.
At base headline() builds the request line without any whitespace check, so a path with an embedded newline is transmitted instead of raising an error.
At head headline() raises RequestError 'Invalid request URI' when the resolved path matches /\s/, so the newline path is rejected before sending.
The PR only changes Albanian (sq) locale scale data and its tests; English million pluralization is untouched, so 1,000,000->'one million' and 2,000,000->'two million' hold at base.
Same reasoning as base: the Albanian-only change does not affect the default English locale, so the English outputs remain correct at head.
The PR only alters saveProperties to tolerate non-String keys; the test uses no custom properties, so singleton resolution returning the same instance is unaffected at base.
Singletons resolve identically at head; the property-loading change is irrelevant when no custom properties are involved.

The refactor is behavior-preserving: replaceElement still appends/swaps/removes and keeps the duplicate-key precondition, so the first replace reorders to (a,1)(z,2)(c,3) and the duplicate-key attempt errors at base.
The shared primitive reproduces the same append/swap/remove steps and the duplicate-key precondition, so results are unchanged at head.
max(cast.ToInt(sizeStr),0) is behavior-identical to the old negative-clamp, and cast.ToInt('-5MB') yields <=0, so both paths return 0 at base.
The refactor is an equivalent clamp (max(...,0)), so '-5MB' still resolves to 0 bytes at head.

At base findCaseInsensitivePathRec uses children[0] for the wildcard, which is a static node when static+param routes share a prefix, so the switch hits default and panics ('invalid node type') on /PREFIX/XXX and /prefix/a/b/c.
The PR falls back to children[len-1] for the wildcard and tries static children first, so /PREFIX/XXX resolves to /prefix/xxx and /prefix/a/b/c returns 404 without panicking.
At base toBigInt returns the nil n.Int when Int is nil and Exp==0, then IsInt64 dereferences it, so Numeric{Valid:true}.Int64Value() panics instead of returning 0.
The PR guards toBigInt to return big.NewInt(0) when Int is nil, so Int64Value (and Float64Value) both report 0 without panicking.
The PR only changes the cursed renderer's tab-stop handling for hard tabs; it does not touch program shutdown/quit logic, so a program quits promptly when quit is called externally at base.
The tab-stop fix is rendering-only and unrelated to quit/shutdown, so the program still returns promptly at head.
At base run_until_cancelled always builds the future and polls the inner op even when already cancelled, so polling the wrapped panic future triggers the panic instead of returning Ready(None).
At head run_until_cancelled checks is_cancelled() first and returns None without polling the inner future, so the already-cancelled case resolves to Ready(None) with no panic.
The PR only optimizes the ignore walker to skip loading unreachable ignore files; case-insensitive literal search matching is unchanged, so all case variants match at base.
The walker change does not affect search matching, so case-insensitive search still finds every case variant at head.

The change only flattens `if let Default::None { if skip { ... } }` into `container_default.is_none() && skip_deserializing...`, which is logically identical, so a skipped-deserializing field still gets its type default at base.
The refactored condition has the same semantics as the original nested check, so skip-deserializing fields still receive their type's default value at head.
